scope: Initial assessment and research opportunities; not a completed worldwide inventory or a dated reconstruction of all ancient coasts.

sources.title: SUBNORDICA: beyond submerged landscapes
sources.note: Official project period: April 2024–March 2030. Uses North Sea and Baltic data to develop methods for identifying archaeological targets.

sources.title: Global sea-level rise in the early Holocene revealed from North Sea peats
sources.note: Hijma et al., 2025. Dated peat sequences, regional land-motion corrections and uncertainty; a route toward a defensible regional reconstruction.

sources.title: North Sea peats: supplementary information and data
sources.note: Repository API checked: CC BY 4.0. Contains the HOLSEA spreadsheet, age-calibration scripts, core photographs, technical documentation and model grids. Files listed; scientific contents not yet independently reanalysed.

sources.title: Major marine archaeological discovery in the Gulf of Cambay and its significance
sources.note: Kathiroli and NIOT colleagues, 2004 conference abstract. Reports sonar patterns, palaeochannel-like features and grab/dredge samples. The source proposes structures; it is not an independent confirmation of that interpretation.

sources.title: Pavlopetri Underwater Archaeology Project: research impact record
sources.note: Documents the project begun in 2009, mapped buildings and ceramics indicating occupation from about 3500 BCE through the Bronze Age. Historical project record; current fieldwork not verified.

sources.title: Pavlopetri: 2010 field report
sources.note: Reports structural survey, sector-scan sonar and stereo photogrammetry. A useful example of multiple recording methods applied to the same identified site.

sources.title: Aboriginal artefacts on the continental shelf reveal ancient drowned cultural landscapes in northwest Australia
sources.note: Benjamin et al., 2020. Reports Cape Bruguieres and Flying Foam Passage, combining remote sensing and diver inspection. Site-formation and sea-level reasoning must accompany the artefact claims.

sources.title: A submerged Stone Age hunting architecture from the Western Baltic Sea
sources.note: Geersen et al., 2024; DOI 10.1073/pnas.2312008121. Hydroacoustic, sediment and optical observations support an anthropogenic wall interpretation. Hunting use and age are contextual inferences.

sources.title: Prehistoric human migration between Sundaland and South Asia was driven by sea-level rise
sources.note: 2023 study combining sea-level and population models. The reconstructed landscape is relevant to targeting; it is not a discovery of a submerged city.

sources.title: Sea level and global ice volumes from the Last Glacial Maximum to the Holocene
sources.note: Lambeck et al., 2014. Global ice-volume and sea-level history distinguishes the glacial maximum from later deglaciation and regional relative sea level.

sources.title: GEBCO_2025 Grid and Type Identifier grid
sources.note: Versioned global 15 arc-second elevation compilation. The TID grid identifies input-data types; spatial grid spacing must not be treated as uniform survey accuracy.

sources.title: EMODnet Bathymetry DTM 2024 release
sources.note: Release announcement dated 24 March 2025. European grid at 1/16 arc-minute spacing, with multiple contributing survey methods.

sources.title: EMODnet DTM 2024: ERDDAP data access
sources.note: Metadata endpoint checked. Variables include elevation, source index, count and interpolation flag; these help audit provenance rather than treating every pixel as measured.

sources.title: NOAA ETOPO1: versioned ERDDAP relief dataset
sources.note: The demonstrator uses small subsamples of this older 2009 global relief model. Four actual NetCDF downloads and hashes are retained. Mean-sea-level elevations; not an ancient coastline model.

sources.title: NCEI Marine Trackline Geophysical Data
sources.note: Searchable bathymetry, sub-bottom, side-scan, magnetic, gravity and seismic records. Coverage and acquisition quality vary by survey; some files require additional handling.

sources.title: ESA: satellite-derived bathymetry
sources.note: Optical shallow-water method sensitive to clarity, clouds, glint and bottom properties. Different from inferring broad seafloor relief through satellite altimetry.

sources.title: Space-borne bathymetry with ICESat-2 and Sentinel-2
sources.note: NASA-hosted 2021 study describes calibration and validation of shallow, clear-water bathymetry. No universal depth limit or archaeological-detection capability is implied.

sources.title: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem
sources.note: Portal for Sentinel observations. This edition links acquisition access; no satellite scene has yet been processed for this programme.

projects.name: Doggerland & the North Sea
projects.label: A landscape we can begin to reconstruct
projects.finding: Peat, buried channels and surveyed landscapes offer a way to recover former environments. SUBNORDICA is developing a systematic route from such evidence to archaeological targets.
projects.limit: A mapped river or dated peat bed does not by itself identify a settlement. Modern seabed relief may overlie a buried land surface.
projects.next: Start with the open sea-level database and source-quality layers; reproduce a regional reconstruction before ranking candidate habitats.

projects.name: Gulf of Khambhat / Cambay
projects.label: A claim that needs its original context
projects.activity: NIOT reports from the early 2000s; a current excavation programme was not verified
projects.precision: regional anchor, not an exact feature position
projects.finding: The proposing researchers report sonar geometries, channel-like features and recovered samples in a strongly dynamic marine setting.
projects.limit: The source’s grab/dredge samples do not, on their own, establish that dated material belongs to a human-built feature. This edition has not independently verified the reported city interpretation.
projects.next: Seek original georeferenced sonar lines, processing history, repeat surveys and sample-context records. Separate a natural-feature test from a chronology test.

projects.name: Pavlopetri, Greece
projects.label: A submerged settlement, recorded in detail
projects.activity: Published survey and excavation programme begun in 2009; ongoing work not asserted
projects.finding: Mapped buildings, streets and ceramics provide archaeological evidence for a settlement spanning the Final Neolithic and Bronze Age.
projects.limit: This is a much later settlement than 12,000 years ago. Its submergence history cannot be applied to every shelf or monument.
projects.next: Use the survey as a positive control for recording methods: which architectural features survive in bathymetry, sonar and diver photography?

projects.name: Murujuga’s submerged country
projects.label: Stone artefacts in a drowned coastal landscape
projects.activity: Deep History of Sea Country research reported in 2020; current field status not checked
projects.finding: The study reports underwater stone artefacts at Cape Bruguieres and a find near a submerged freshwater feature at Flying Foam Passage, using remote sensing and diver investigation.
projects.limit: Transport, erosion and site formation matter. The inferred exposure history is not direct dating of every stone artefact.
projects.next: Follow the published landscape-prediction method and engage the relevant Traditional Owners before any field-oriented extension.

projects.name: The Baltic stone alignment
projects.label: A testable interpretation beneath 21 metres of water
projects.finding: A roughly kilometre-long stone alignment was recorded using hydroacoustic surveys, optical imagery and sediment evidence. The authors interpret it as prehistoric hunting architecture.
projects.limit: The existence and layout of stones are observations. Hunting function and the timing of construction depend on contextual arguments.
projects.next: Compare the arrangement with natural glacial features and inspect the dated surrounding sediment sequence, not just the striking sonar image.

projects.name: The Sunda shelf
projects.label: A very large landscape with a much thinner archaeological record
projects.activity: Published sea-level and population modelling, including a 2023 study
projects.finding: Lower sea levels exposed extensive shelf areas between today’s islands. Published modelling explores connections between inundation and population history.
projects.limit: Exposed terrain is not evidence of a lost city or of one connected civilisation. Local preservation, sediment burial and survey coverage remain decisive.
projects.next: Identify accessible seismic and sediment datasets, then test palaeochannels and freshwater margins against a dated regional model.

datasets.name: North Sea sea-level records
datasets.resolution: Dated point observations, uncertainty, core logs and model grids
datasets.access: CC BY 4.0 repository; file list and licence checked
datasets.use: Reproduce regional relative sea-level constraints, distinguish limiting points from index points, and propagate age/elevation uncertainty.
datasets.limit: The scientific spreadsheets and grids have not yet been independently reanalysed here. Some grids are large; start with the database and documentation.

datasets.name: GEBCO_2025 + source types
datasets.resolution: 15 arc-second grid spacing; effective survey resolution varies
datasets.access: Open downloads and regional subsets under GEBCO terms
datasets.use: Screen shelf morphology and inspect the Type Identifier layer before deciding where higher-quality data are needed.
datasets.limit: A fine-looking grid can incorporate inferred or interpolated depths. It cannot resolve or authenticate small archaeological structures by itself.

datasets.name: EMODnet DTM 2024
datasets.coverage: European seas, plus a separate Caribbean product
datasets.access: Open portal and ERDDAP; service metadata checked
datasets.use: Combine elevations with source indices and interpolation flags. Search for finer contributing surveys around a chosen study area.
datasets.limit: Datum, interpolation, acquisition dates and effective resolution need checking. Modern depths alone are not buried palaeotopography.

datasets.name: NCEI survey and trackline archive
datasets.resolution: Survey-specific: single/multibeam, sonar and seismic products
datasets.access: Searchable archive with downloadable formats; inspect each cruise’s metadata
datasets.use: Locate actual survey lines and sub-bottom records, distinguish measured coverage from a seamless-looking global basemap.
datasets.limit: A catalogue hit is not yet an analysis-ready dataset. Navigation, instruments, processing and time/depth conversion can matter.

datasets.name: Sentinel-2 + ICESat-2 opportunities
datasets.resolution: Sensor- and method-specific; optical pixels are not depth accuracy
datasets.access: Sentinel portal linked; method papers checked; no local scenes processed yet
datasets.use: Pilot shallow-water depth estimation where water clarity and validation soundings make it appropriate.
datasets.limit: Cloud, turbidity, glint, depth and bottom reflectance limit optical recovery. This is not a method to see through arbitrary deep or muddy water.

datasets.name: This explorer’s retained relief grids
datasets.coverage: World, North Sea, Sunda and Gujarat subsets
datasets.resolution: Subsampled ETOPO1: 20′ global; 3′ North Sea; 6′ Sunda; 2′ Gujarat
datasets.access: Actual downloaded NetCDF source files retained; compact grids and hashes published
datasets.use: Understand shelf geometry and explore how changing a depth threshold alters the area highlighted.
datasets.limit: Older 2009 relief compilation; deliberately coarse. It is an orientation tool, not a dated shoreline or an archaeological detector.
